items.title: Funnel waterfall — teach the journey, don't just say 'warming'
items.why: The /status/ Conversion funnel tile shows '1 / 20 events measured' and nothing else. Even in the honest-dark state, the tile can show the five journey stages (Visit → Proof seen → Dispatch shown → Subscribe → Membership) as a horizontal waterfall with 'awaiting data' placeholders. This transforms a passive wait indicator into active transparency — visitors see exactly what the studio measures and why. The waterfall fills in with real rates when minSamples is reached.
items.recipe: In status/index.html extend the funnel tile render: when honestDark=true, render 5 labeled stages with '—' counts in a .funnel-waterfall container; when live, fill in real rates. Stages: Visit, proof-line:shown, studio-dispatch:subscribe (terminal), oracle-chip:click, Membership. CSS: flex row with connecting arrows via ::before pseudo, gold highlight on populated stages.

items.title: Session velocity badge — animate the 189-session proof
items.why: The honest-traction scoreboard shows sessions as a static number. The velocity is the story: 189 sessions in ~189 days is a rare solo-studio cadence. Framing it as 'avg 1 per day' with an animated count-up on first scroll + 'Last session: today' turns a static fact into a felt signal. Also fixes the 1-session staleness: public-intelligence.json sessionsCompleted=188, not 189.
items.recipe: Update public-intelligence.json sync to pull sessionsCompleted from context/SELF_IMPROVEMENT_LOOP.md Rolling Status header at build time. In honest-traction-scoreboard.js: (1) add IntersectionObserver-triggered count-up animation (requestAnimationFrame, 800ms); (2) add 'Last session: N days ago' meta label from public-intelligence.json updatedAt; (3) add 'avg 1/day' framing when sessions/days > 0.7. No new external deps.

items.title: Progressive membership unlock — stage-matched nudges from real visit signals
items.why: The membership page shows identical copy to a cold first-timer and a fifth-visit returning visitor. returning-visitor-digest.js already tracks visit count in localStorage; proof-conversion-line.js fires a beacon on proof interaction. These are the two strongest pre-purchase signals on the site. A progressive disclosure system that reads those signals and adjusts the membership card copy — Stage 1 (cold), Stage 2 (returning), Stage 3 (proof-engaged), Stage 4 (dispatch subscriber) — turns a static pitch into a natural escalating conversation.
items.recipe: Create assets/membership-unlock.js (deferred, CSP-safe): read vs_visit_count from localStorage + vs_proof_seen flag + footer-dispatch cookie. Set data-vs-unlock-stage=[1-4] on the #mem-interview-mount container. CSS attribute selectors show stage-matched elements. Wire allowlisted 'membership-unlock:stage-N' beacons (check-rum-allowlist both ends).

items.why: The current journal/_drafts/forge-week-2026-06-11.md contains verbatim task-board entries like '[S186][UX/P0] PROOF-TO-CONVERSION-BRIDGE — DONE.' — internal shorthand, not studio voice. check-content-freshness.mjs warns on 82+ day journal staleness every session. Improving draft-weekly-forge.mjs to translate Done-item slugs into plain-English SOUL-voice sentences means the founder can publish with a read-through, not a full rewrite. The journal is a direct engagement surface for Vault Members.

items.title: Auto-derive changelog from TASK_BOARD Done — kill the 59-day staleness
items.why: The /changelog/ page hasn't been updated in 59 days. check-content-freshness.mjs warns every session but the fix is manual. The TASK_BOARD Done section has every shipped item in structured format. A script that reads the most recent 30-60 days of Done entries and generates a structured changelog section (grouped by session, cleaned of internal shorthand) makes content freshness a solved problem, not a recurring founder-action. Changelog freshness is a direct SEO and trust signal.

items.title: Proof embed card — let the status proof travel outside the site
items.why: api/status-proof.json publishes trustScore, LCP, uptime, and deploy field-wins as machine-readable proof used exclusively within the site. A copyable embed snippet (<script src='/assets/proof-card.js'></script>) gives the studio a trust-distribution surface: the card can embed in third-party pages, press kit emails, Discord descriptions. It reads from the deployed JSON, renders in ~40 lines of vanilla JS. No indie studio does this.
items.recipe: Create assets/proof-card.js (standalone, no deps): reads /api/status-proof.json, renders a 240px inline card (LCP, uptime %, session count, trust tier) with VS branding link. Self-contained CSS, respects prefers-color-scheme. On /status/ add a 'Share this proof' toggle section showing the embed code + a preview render. Wire proof-card:embed beacon (check-rum-allowlist).

items.title: Oracle seed chips — adapt to helpful-feedback signal instead of staying static
items.why: The 3 cold-start chips on the Oracle page (S186) are drawn from static oracle-insights.json clusters. The oracle-answer:helpful/unhelpful feedback loop (S189) now fires signals identifying which query-class resonates. Re-ranking chips by recency-weighted helpful-rate turns the cold-start into a self-improving surface. Even re-ranking once per session (reading oracle-insights.json sorted by recent helpful signals) is a meaningful improvement over static order.
items.recipe: In the chip-rendering path of ignis-engine.js: after loading oracle-insights.json, sort clusters by recency-weighted helpful-rate proxy (join data/rum-ux-history.ndjson oracle-answer:helpful entries by approximate time window; fallback to static order). Expose data-vs-chip-rank on each chip. Wire oracle-chip:adaptive-shown beacon (add to Worker RUM_UX_EVENTS + check-rum-allowlist).

items.title: Oracle quality loop — flag low-helpful clusters for next IGNIS rescore
items.why: The 👍/👎 oracle-answer feedback fires to /v/rum but never completes the loop — IGNIS re-scoring doesn't read the helpful-rate. When a query cluster consistently generates unhelpful answers, it should flag for the next rescore cycle. A lightweight data/oracle-feedback.ndjson appended by rollup-rum-ux.mjs gives IGNIS a quality signal it currently lacks.
items.recipe: In scripts/rollup-rum-ux.mjs: when processing oracle-answer family, if unhelpful count > 2 within the window, append an entry to data/oracle-feedback.ndjson with {date, unhelpfulCount, helpfulCount, flagged: true}. Add check-funnel-contract validation: oracle-feedback.ndjson entries must have required fields. Self-test case added.
